records.title: Steering Damper Wear Causing Wander and Vibration
records.description: The recirculating ball steering system on W463 G-Class models relies on a steering damper that wears out over time, causing excessive highway wander, steering wheel vibration at speed, and a vague on-center feel. The solid front axle design amplifies these symptoms compared to independent suspension vehicles.
records.solution: Replace the steering damper with an OEM or upgraded aftermarket unit such as Bilstein B6. Inspect the drag link and tie rod ends for play simultaneously. Perform a front-end alignment after replacement.
symptoms: Clunking over bumps from front end

records.title: Air Suspension Compressor Failure
records.description: The AIRMATIC compressor fails prematurely on the GLE, typically after one or more air springs develop slow leaks. The heavy SUV puts more stress on the compressor than sedan applications, accelerating wear.
records.solution: Replace the compressor and relay. Leak-test all four air springs and replace any that are leaking. The compressor runs $400-800 for aftermarket (Arnott) or $1,200+ OEM.
symptoms: Vehicle drops to lowest position overnight

records.title: DCT Transmission Shudder
records.description: The 8G-DCT dual-clutch transmission develops a shudder during low-speed acceleration, similar to driving over rumble strips. The clutch packs overheat in stop-and-go traffic, causing judder and vibration during engagement.
records.solution: Update the DCT software to the latest calibration. In persistent cases, the clutch assembly may need replacement. Avoid prolonged creeping in traffic — use the brake instead of riding the clutch at low speed.
symptoms: Vibration at low speeds similar to rumble strips

citations.title: MBWorld.org - W177 A-Class DCT shudder complaints and clutch replacement discussion

communityRecommendations.content: Use Sport mode or manual mode in heavy traffic. This delays upshifts and keeps the DCT from hunting between 1st and 2nd gear, reducing clutch wear.

records.title: MBUX Infotainment Software Bugs
records.description: The MBUX infotainment system suffers from frequent software bugs including touchscreen lag, voice assistant failures ("Hey Mercedes" not responding), Bluetooth disconnects, and navigation freezes. The A-Class was the first Mercedes model with MBUX and received early software that was less polished.
records.solution: Visit a Mercedes dealer for the latest MBUX over-the-air update. Factory reset the MBUX system (Settings > System > Reset). Re-pair all Bluetooth devices from scratch after the update.
symptoms: Hey Mercedes voice assistant does not respond

citations.title: MBWorld.org - A-Class MBUX software update tracker and bug report thread

communityRecommendations.content: Check for MBUX updates quarterly. Mercedes pushes silent OTA updates but they sometimes require a dealer visit to install major version changes.

records.title: Front Suspension Strut Noise
records.description: The front MacPherson struts develop a clunking or knocking noise over bumps and rough surfaces. The strut mount bearing wears prematurely, and the strut itself can develop internal valving noise. More common on vehicles with AMG suspension.
records.solution: Replace the front strut mount bearings first ($100-200 per side). If the noise persists, replace the strut assemblies. Use OEM or Sachs (OEM supplier) replacement struts for proper ride quality.
symptoms: Clunking noise from front over bumps
Knocking when turning at low speed

citations.title: MBWorld.org - W177 A-Class front strut noise diagnosis and replacement

communityRecommendations.content: Have the strut mount bearings checked first — they are the most common cause and cheapest to replace. Most shops go straight to full strut replacement unnecessarily.

records.title: 48V Mild-Hybrid Battery Degradation and Faults
records.description: The 48V EQ Boost mild-hybrid system battery in AMG GT 43 and GT 53 models degrades prematurely, causing reduced electric assist, ISG (Integrated Starter-Generator) faults, and inability to use electric auxiliary functions. The E Performance plug-in models can also experience 48V system faults separate from the main high-voltage battery.
records.solution: Diagnose the 48V battery state of health with Mercedes Star Diagnostics. If capacity has dropped below threshold, replace the 48V lithium-ion battery pack located in the engine bay. Software calibration is required after battery replacement.

citations.title: MBWorld.org — AMG GT 4-Door 48V EQ Boost system faults and battery replacement reports

communityRecommendations.content: If the 48V battery fails out of warranty, expect $2,000-$3,000 for replacement. The battery is separate from the main 12V battery and requires dealer-level diagnostics to properly calibrate.

records.title: Air Suspension Compressor Failure
records.description: The AMG GT 4-Door Coupe equipped with AMG Ride Control+ air suspension experiences premature compressor failures. The compressor overworks to maintain the low ride height and firm damping settings, leading to overheating and eventual burnout. Failure results in the vehicle dropping to its lowest ride height with no ability to adjust.
records.solution: Replace the air suspension compressor. Inspect air springs for leaks that may have caused the compressor to overwork. Update the suspension control module software to the latest version which includes improved compressor duty-cycle management.
symptoms: Vehicle sitting low and unable to raise
Ride height uneven side to side
Unable to select Sport or Comfort modes

citations.title: MBWorld.org — AMG GT 4-Door air suspension compressor failure reports X290

communityRecommendations.content: If you notice the compressor running longer than normal after starting the car, get it checked immediately. An overworking compressor is usually compensating for a slow air leak and will burn out.

records.title: Rear Axle Steering System Fault
records.description: The optional rear-axle steering system on AMG GT 63 models develops faults where the rear steering actuator fails or the control module loses communication. When this occurs, the system defaults to a locked center position and displays a steering fault warning. The feature becomes inoperable and the car handles differently than expected at low speeds.
records.solution: Diagnose with Mercedes Star Diagnostics to identify the specific fault — actuator motor, position sensor, or control module. Software updates can resolve some faults. Physical actuator replacement requires rear subframe work and a four-wheel alignment afterward.
symptoms: Rear axle steering fault warning on dashboard
Vehicle feels less agile at low speeds

citations.title: MBWorld.org — AMG GT 4-Door rear axle steering fault diagnosis and repair thread

communityRecommendations.content: Many rear-axle steering faults are resolved with a software update. Always try the software approach first before authorizing expensive actuator replacement.

records.title: Active Transaxle Mount Connectivity Faults and Replacement
records.description: The C190 AMG GT mounts its rear transaxle on three ACTIVE (electronically controlled) mounts that stiffen under hard cornering and soften at idle. The most common reported failure isn't rubber breakdown — it's wiring harness or connector corrosion at the mount sensors, which trips dash warnings ("Suspension malfunction" / "Engine/transmission mount fault") and forces the mounts into a default-soft state. The fix is usually harness cleaning or connector replacement; full mount replacement is uncommon but expensive when needed (active mounts are pricey OEM parts and labor at the rear of the car is significant). The original entry incorrectly described these as passive hydraulic mounts.
records.solution: Replace the transaxle mounts with updated Mercedes parts. Inspect the torque tube bearing simultaneously. Use OEM mounts unless the car is tracked, in which case solid mounts from aftermarket suppliers may be preferred.
symptoms: Vibration through cabin at low speed
Harsh engagement when going from park to drive

citations.title: MBWorld.org — AMG GT transaxle mount wear and replacement procedure

communityRecommendations.content: Track use accelerates mount wear dramatically. If you track your AMG GT, inspect the transaxle mounts every 15,000 miles.

records.title: Dual-Clutch Transmission (DCT) Shudder at Low Speeds
records.description: The 7-speed dual-clutch transmission (7G-DCT) in the B-Class develops a noticeable shudder during low-speed maneuvers and from a standstill. The issue stems from clutch pack wear and adaptive software that struggles to compensate as the clutch material thins over time.
records.solution: Start with a DCT adaptation reset via Mercedes XENTRY diagnostic tool. If shudder persists, the dual-clutch assembly requires replacement. Updated clutch packs with revised friction material are available and significantly improve longevity.

citations.title: MBWorld.org — B-Class DCT shudder and clutch replacement discussion thread

communityRecommendations.content: A transmission adaptation reset often buys time, but the clutch pack will eventually need replacement. Budget for it around 60,000-80,000 miles.

records.title: Electric Drive Motor Whine and Bearing Noise (B250e)
records.description: The B250e electric drive unit produces an abnormal high-pitched whine or growling noise that increases with speed. The noise originates from worn bearings in the electric motor or the single-speed reduction gear. Tesla supplied the drivetrain components, and parts availability has become limited.
records.solution: Diagnose whether the noise is from the motor bearings or reduction gear. Motor bearing replacement is possible at specialized EV shops. If the reduction gear is worn, the entire drive unit may need replacement. Check with Mercedes for remaining parts availability as the B250e is discontinued.
symptoms: High-pitched whine that increases with speed
Noise changes character with regenerative braking

citations.title: MBWorld.org — B250e electric drive motor noise diagnosis and parts sourcing

communityRecommendations.content: Parts for the B250e are becoming scarce since the Tesla-sourced drivetrain is discontinued. Address noise early before bearing damage becomes catastrophic and destroys the motor.

records.title: Turbocharger Oil Feed Line Leak
records.description: The turbo oil feed line on the M270 engine in the B-Class develops leaks at the banjo bolt connection on top of the turbocharger. Oil drips onto the hot exhaust manifold, producing a burning oil smell and visible smoke from the engine bay.
records.solution: Replace the turbo oil feed line and both copper crush washers at the banjo bolt connections. Inspect the turbo for bearing play while the line is disconnected. Clean oil residue from the exhaust manifold to eliminate the burning smell.
symptoms: Burning oil smell from engine bay

citations.title: MBWorld.org — B250 M270 turbo oil leak repair with part numbers

communityRecommendations.content: Oil on a hot exhaust manifold is a fire risk. Address the leak promptly and monitor oil level weekly until repaired.

records.title: A/C Drain Hose Water Ingress into Footwell (Electrical/SRS Damage)
records.description: The air conditioning condensate drain hose may not be installed to specification, allowing water to drain into the driver/passenger footwells or center tunnel instead of overboard. Pooled water corrodes and short-circuits electrical control modules in the floor area (SAM, fuel pump control unit, occupancy/SRS sensors). This is NHTSA recall 20V416000 (MB campaign 2020070013), but owners also report wet carpets and module faults outside the recall range.
records.solution: Covered by recall: dealer inspects A/C drain hose installation and corrects routing, installs a water drain plug, and replaces the fuel pump control unit if water-damaged, free of charge. For non-recall water ingress: re-route/replace the drain hose (part A1678323600), dry the carpet/insulation, and replace any corroded modules.

records.title: Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) Blockage and Limp Mode on Short Trips
records.description: On diesel A-Class models (A180d/A200d/A220d, OM608/OM654 engines) driven mainly on short, low-speed urban trips, the DPF cannot reach the high exhaust temperatures needed for passive regeneration. Soot accumulates, the DPF/engine warning light illuminates, and the car can enter limp mode with a stored 'soot content too high' fault. A very common complaint among EU-spec city-driven diesels.
records.solution: First remedy is a sustained highway run (15-30 min at higher rpm) to trigger active regeneration. If that fails, a workshop performs a forced/static regeneration via diagnostics. Severely clogged filters require professional DPF cleaning or replacement. Maintaining EGR valve, turbo, and injectors and using correct spec diesel reduces recurrence.

records.title: Front Axle Integral Carrier Corrosion (Steering Loss Risk)
records.description: The integral carrier (front subframe component) that supports the front axle can corrode due to a manufacturing defect in which the parts did not receive proper corrosion protection. records.solution: Covered by recall: an authorized Mercedes-Benz dealer inspects the integral carrier and replaces it as necessary, free of charge. Owners with a VIN in the affected range should contact a dealer to confirm whether the remedy has been performed; out-of-recall vehicles showing corrosion need subframe/integral carrier replacement.

records.title: M282 1.3L Intake Valve Carbon Buildup
records.description: The 1.3L turbocharged direct-injection M282 engine (co-developed with Renault, used in A180/A200) suffers carbon deposit buildup on the intake valves and ports because direct injection does not wash the valve backs with fuel. On urban/short-trip duty cycles deposits accumulate from roughly 60,000 miles, causing rough running and hesitation.
records.solution: Walnut-shell media blasting of the intake valves/ports, typically recommended every ~50,000-60,000 miles. Using top-tier fuel, periodic intake/induction cleaning, and avoiding constant short trips slows buildup. A quality oil meeting the MB spec helps limit blow-by contribution.

records.title: M282 Thermostat Housing / Coolant Leak
records.description: The 1.3L M282 engine develops coolant leaks at the integrated thermostat housing/gasket and at the water pump and coolant hoses, commonly in the 55,000-70,000 mile range. A failing thermostat housing causes temperature gauge fluctuation, coolant loss, and slow cabin heating; if ignored it can lead to overheating. Coolant leaks are repeatedly cited as one of the most common cooling-system issues on A 250/A 200 owners.
records.solution: Replace the complete OEM thermostat housing assembly (it is plastic and integrated, so the full unit is required), inspect/replace water pump and coolant hoses, then refill and bleed the cooling system with the correct MB-spec coolant. Address promptly to avoid overheating damage.

records.title: 12V Battery Drain from Telematics / Sleep-Mode Module Wakes (Platform-Wide Pattern)
records.description: Mercedes' current electronic architecture (shared across the C192 AMG GT, W206 C-Class, X254 GLC, and EQE/EQS) has documented 12V battery drain complaints from control modules not sleeping properly — typically the telematics / mbrace head unit polling cellular at idle. On the AMG GT specifically, there's no model-specific TSB yet, but the same root cause applies: cars left parked for 1-2+ weeks may need a jump-start, and battery management warnings can appear on the cluster. The W206 has a TSB (LI54.10-P-076820); EQE/EQS got a 2024 software recall (24V-372). Typical remedy on AMG GT is a software update at the dealer or, if the battery has been damaged by repeated deep discharge, replacement (~$400-600 for the AGM unit). Most cases are nuisance-level; severity downgraded from medium to low for that reason.
records.solution: Perform a parasitic draw test after the vehicle times out, then scan all body, telematics, and gateway modules for wake-up events or software faults. Dealers often address this with software updates, battery testing/replacement, and in some cases replacement of a module that remains awake. Owners who store the car or drive infrequently often use a maintainer to prevent repeat discharge while the root cause is being resolved.

communityRecommendations.content: Use a quality AGM-compatible battery maintainer if the car sits for more than a week while diagnosis is ongoing.
Request a printed parasitic-draw test result from the dealer; it helps distinguish a weak battery from a module that is not sleeping.

records.title: MBUX Instrument Cluster Blackout / Reboot While Driving (NHTSA Recall, May 2026)
records.description: An infotainment control unit software defect in 2024-2026 AMG GT (and shared across the C-Class, E-Class, SL, CLE, and GLC on the same platform) can trigger system resets that briefly black out the digital instrument cluster while the vehicle is in motion — hiding speed, warnings, and gear position for several seconds. Mercedes-Benz issued an NHTSA recall covering 144,049 vehicles on May 8, 2026, classifying the defect as safety-critical due to the elevated crash risk during a cluster blackout. The remedy is a free software update at the dealer (or OTA where supported). Owners typically notice MBUX freezes or full reboots while driving before the cluster blanking event; the two symptoms share the same root cause.
records.solution: Confirm battery voltage is stable, then scan for communication faults in the MBUX, telematics, and display modules. Dealers typically perform software updates, SCN coding, or module resets; persistent failures may require replacement of the display/control unit or related communication hardware. If the issue occurs after over-the-air updates, a full dealer reflash is often more effective than repeated resets.
symptoms: Touch inputs lag or stop responding

communityRecommendations.content: Ask the dealer to check for the latest MBUX and instrument-cluster software rather than only performing a battery reset.
If the screen fails intermittently, record a short video showing startup behavior and whether the backup camera/audio are also affected.

records.title: Rear-Axle Steering / Driver Assistance Warning Messages from Chassis Sensor Calibration Faults
records.description: The 2024+ AMG GT uses rear-axle steering and a dense network of chassis sensors tied into stability control and driver assistance systems. Early-owner reports describe warning messages for steering assist, ESP, or driver assistance functions, sometimes after alignment work, low battery events, or software glitches. In many cases the hardware is intact, but calibration values or sensor initialization are lost or out of range.
records.solution: Scan the steering, ESP, and rear-axle steering modules for stored faults, then verify alignment and ride-height values before recalibrating steering-angle and chassis sensors. Dealers commonly perform software updates and guided calibrations; if faults return, they inspect wheel-speed sensors, steering rack/rear-steer actuators, and wiring. A low-voltage event should be ruled out first because it can trigger multiple false chassis warnings.
symptoms: Multiple chassis warnings after low battery

communityRecommendations.content: Do not skip post-alignment calibration on cars with rear-axle steering; several owners report warnings after tire or alignment work.
If multiple chassis warnings appear at once, test battery voltage first before authorizing expensive steering hardware replacement.

records.title: Electronic Parking Brake Actuator Malfunction
records.description: W246 owners report the electronic parking brake (EPB) sticking or showing a malfunction warning on the dashboard. The fault is typically a failing parking-brake actuator motor, corroded cables/connectors, or a software glitch in the control module. The brake may fail to release, refuse to apply, or trigger an EPB warning, which can immobilize the car or require service before driving.
records.solution: Fault-read the EPB control module with XENTRY/STAR. Inspect and clean cabling and connectors, update/recalibrate the EPB control-module software if a glitch is found, and replace the parking-brake actuator motor if it has failed. Recalibrate the system after any actuator or cable replacement.

records.title: M270 Timing Chain Stretch and Cold-Start Rattle (Petrol)
records.description: The turbo petrol M270 (and naturally-aspirated M270/M274 in B180/B200/B250) uses a two-stage timing chain whose plastic guide rails and hydraulic tensioner degrade prematurely. Owners report a loud metallic rattle for roughly 1-15 seconds on cold start that fades as oil pressure builds. Short-trip urban use accelerates the problem because the cold-start period (low oil pressure) makes up a large share of running time. Stretch typically appears from ~80,000 km (50,000 mi), with some city cars rattling from ~70,000 km. Left unaddressed, chain stretch alters valve timing, throws fault codes, and risks contact/wear on cam bearings and phasers.
records.solution: Diagnose with a cold-start listen and read live chain/cam-position data via XENTRY. If only the tensioner is at fault, replacing the hydraulic chain tensioner first is the cheaper initial fix; if the chain is stretched, replace the complete OEM timing kit (chain, both guide rails, tensioner, and cam phaser sprockets if worn) to avoid consequential damage. Use the correct MB-Approval 229.5/229.51 0W-40 or 5W-40 oil and shorten oil-change intervals on short-trip cars.
symptoms: Metallic rattle on cold start lasting 1-15 seconds

records.title: OM651 Diesel DPF and EGR Clogging (B180 CDI / B200 CDI)
records.description: The 2.2L OM651 diesel in B180 CDI / B200 CDI variants is prone to diesel particulate filter (DPF) blockage and EGR-valve carbon fouling, especially on short urban trips where the exhaust never reaches regeneration temperature. Symptoms include reduced power (limp mode), increased fuel consumption, frequent failed regenerations, and warning lights. Carbon buildup in the EGR valve and intake also causes hesitation and rough running. The OM651 timing chain can also stretch and rattle, compounding diesel reliability concerns.
records.solution: Take the car for sustained high-speed driving to allow a complete regeneration; if the DPF is heavily loaded, perform a forced regen via XENTRY or a professional DPF clean, and in severe cases replace the DPF. Clean or replace a fouled EGR valve and clear intake carbon. Read soot-load and differential-pressure data to confirm. Diagnose and fix any underlying cause (failed glow plugs, leaking injectors, faulty differential-pressure sensor) before replacing the filter. Maintain with correct low-SAPS oil and longer drive cycles.

records.title: Panoramic Sunroof Drain Clog and Water Leak
records.description: W246 cars fitted with the panoramic glass roof suffer water ingress when the front-corner sunroof drain tubes clog with leaves and debris, or when the perimeter rubber seal wears. Owners report water entering at the front edge / A-pillar area and pooling in the footwell, with damp carpet, headliner staining, and musty smells. The drains are located at the right and left front of the sunroof. Trapped water can also reach electrical modules under the carpet.
records.solution: Inspect and flush the four sunroof drain tubes with low-pressure compressed air or a gentle water stream to clear debris; verify water exits at the rocker/sill outlets. Inspect and replace the perimeter sunroof seal if cracked, shrunken, or deformed. Dry the carpet/headliner and check underfloor connectors for corrosion. Periodic drain cleaning is the key preventive step.

records.title: Plastic Thermostat Housing Coolant Leak (M270)
records.description: The M270/M274 petrol engines use a map-controlled, electronically actuated thermostat integrated into a plastic housing that cracks or warps with age and heat cycling, becoming a common slow coolant-leak point. Early symptoms are a sweet coolant smell from the engine bay and a gradually dropping coolant level with no visible puddle (it evaporates on hot surfaces), plus temperature-gauge fluctuation or slow warm-up as the thermostat starts sticking. On a cold-day test drive the car should reach ~80 C within 10-15 minutes; if it hovers below, suspect the thermostat. It is an expensive, dealer-favored repair because of access.
records.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the thermostat housing for seepage. Replace the complete thermostat/housing assembly with the genuine Mercedes part (aftermarket replicas have a high repeat-failure rate on M270), refill with the correct MB-spec coolant, and bleed the system. Address any concurrent water-pump weep-hole leak at the same time.
symptoms: Sweet coolant smell from engine bay
Slowly dropping coolant with no visible puddle
Slow warm-up / engine not reaching ~80 C

records.title: Tailgate / Boot Lock Actuator Electrical Failure
records.description: The W246 tailgate (boot) locking system is a frequently reported electrical weak point. Corroded contacts in the lock actuator, a defective interior release lever, or water ingress from a leaking rear-washer hose cause the boot to fail to open or lock. Keyless-Go interaction and a weak key battery can compound the symptom. Electrical faults account for a large share of W246 complaints, and the tailgate lock is among the most-cited. The emergency release cable behind the rear seat backrest is the temporary workaround when the boot will not open.
records.solution: Clean the actuator contacts with electrical contact cleaner and apply dielectric grease (preventive cleaning roughly every 30,000 km is advised). Repair or re-solder corroded wiring (a Mercedes repair kit with heat-shrink is commonly used). For a permanently defective actuator, replace the lock actuator and re-teach the component via XENTRY. Fix any leaking rear-washer hose that allows water into the lock mechanism, and dry/clean affected connectors.
symptoms: Boot/tailgate will not open from button or key

records.title: 48V Mild-Hybrid / Integrated Starter-Generator Failure Causing No-Start and Power Loss
records.description: The W206 C-Class uses a 48V mild-hybrid system with an integrated starter-generator (ISG), and owners have reported no-start conditions, repeated warning messages, charging-system faults, and sudden reduced-power events tied to the 48V system. Mercedes has issued service information and field actions on related hybrid electrical faults across current models using this architecture, and owner complaints describe vehicles becoming undriveable or requiring towing. Failures can involve the ISG itself, DC/DC conversion, wiring, or software/calibration issues that trigger shutdowns and battery warnings.
records.solution: A proper diagnosis requires scanning both the 48V and 12V systems, checking state of charge, converter operation, and fault history in the powertrain and hybrid control modules. Repairs may include software updates, replacement of the integrated starter-generator or associated power electronics, and battery/module adaptation after installation. Because the system is high-current and model-specific, independent repair options are limited compared with dealer service.
symptoms: engine shuts off or will not restart after auto stop/start

communityRecommendations.content: If a no-start follows auto stop/start or a 48V warning, have the vehicle scanned before repeated jump-start attempts; repeated low-voltage events can muddy the root cause.
Owners often recommend keeping copies of all warning-message photos and tow invoices because intermittent 48V faults may require multiple dealer visits.

records.title: 722.6 5G-Tronic conductor plate failure (limp mode, stuck in 2nd gear)
records.description: The 722.6 five-speed automatic (fitted to W202 facelift cars from ~1996 onward and all 2001-2002 W203s) uses an electronic conductor plate mounted on top of the valve body that integrates the speed sensors and routes signals to the solenoids. The plate fails for two reasons: (1) the internal RPM sensors get coated by ferrous wear particles when the fluid is never changed, producing implausible-slip codes, and (2) the soldered traces and embedded capacitor crack from heat cycling. Failure puts the transmission into limp-home mode — stuck in 2nd gear, harsh 1-2 and 2-3 shifts, or no upshift at all. Often accompanied by codes P0717, P0720, P0731-P0736 and a transmission warning light. This is the single most common 722.6 failure across every Mercedes chassis that uses it.
records.solution: Replace the conductor plate (Mercedes p/n A140 270 13 61 or supersession). The 722.6 conductor plate is plug-and-play with no coding required (unlike the later 722.9). Always replace the 13-pin pilot bushing/connector adapter at the same time — ATF wicks up through the old one and ruins the TCM. Do a full fluid and filter change while the pan is off. DIY kit + plate runs $250-450 in parts; shop labor adds $400-800. Continuing to drive in limp mode can damage clutches and turn this into a $3000+ rebuild.
symptoms: Transmission warning light or wrench icon
Speedometer drops to 0 intermittently while driving
Fluid on the 13-pin transmission electrical connector

records.title: Biodegradable engine wiring harness insulation breakdown (M104/M111/M119)
records.description: Mercedes-Benz used environmentally-friendly biodegradable wiring insulation in engine harnesses from 1993-1995 across the W202 C-Class, W124 E-Class, W140 S-Class, and R129 SL. The insulation becomes brittle from underhood heat cycling, cracks, falls off, and exposes bare copper conductors. This causes intermittent shorts, no-start conditions, random misfires, check engine lights with multiple sensor codes simultaneously, and in worst cases engine bay fires. The M111 four-cylinder cars have a separate ignition harness that also fails. The M104 inline-six (3.2L variants) and the M119 V8 are particularly affected; the later M104 3.0L versions used updated insulation. Damage is visible as crumbling brown/black insulation around injector connectors, MAF, throttle body, and coil packs.
records.solution: The only permanent fix is full engine harness replacement with the redesigned post-1996 harness using conventional insulation. OEM Mercedes harnesses (e.g. 1244403633 / 2024407505) are available but expensive. Specialist re-pinning/refurbishment services (ClassicMercedes.co.uk, R129.co) rebuild the existing harness with new wire for less. DIY heat-shrink repair of individual wires is a short-term band-aid only; the insulation will continue degrading elsewhere on the loom.
symptoms: Crumbling, cracked, or missing wire insulation visible on engine harness
Multiple simultaneous fault codes (injectors, MAF, O2 sensors, coils)
Check engine light that comes and goes
Visible bare copper wire at connectors

records.title: Driver Assistance Sensor Misalignment Causing 'Inoperative' Warnings and Disabled Features
records.description: Owners of 2022-2025 C-Class cars frequently report sudden warnings that Active Brake Assist, Distronic, lane-keeping, blind-spot monitoring, or parking sensors are inoperative. On the W206, these faults are often tied to radar/camera calibration sensitivity, software issues, or sensor obstruction/misalignment after minor impacts, windshield work, or even routine driving in poor weather. The result is a cluster of driver-assistance features dropping offline until the system is recalibrated or updated.
records.solution: The vehicle should be scanned for camera, radar, and ADAS communication faults, then inspected for dirty sensor faces, bumper damage, windshield replacement history, and alignment issues. Many cases are resolved with software updates and static/dynamic calibration of the front camera or radar sensors; damaged brackets or sensors must be replaced before calibration. Battery voltage should also be verified because low voltage can trigger multiple false ADAS warnings.
symptoms: multiple driver assistance warnings at once

communityRecommendations.content: After windshield replacement or front-end repair, owners recommend confirming that ADAS calibration was actually performed, not just sensor installation.
Keep radar covers and camera areas clean, but if warnings recur in clear weather, request a calibration report and software version printout from the dealer.

records.title: Front Seat Occupant Classification / Passenger Airbag Warning Faults
records.description: Multiple W206 owners have reported passenger restraint warnings, inoperative passenger airbag indicators, and seat-related fault messages shortly after purchase. These complaints align with Mercedes service actions and owner reports involving seat occupancy detection mats/sensors, seat wiring, or control-module calibration issues. Because the system determines passenger airbag deployment logic, faults can trigger warning lights and require immediate diagnosis.
records.solution: Diagnosis should include scanning the supplemental restraint system for seat-occupancy and seat-module faults, inspecting under-seat connectors/wiring, and checking for applicable software updates or service campaigns. Repairs may involve recalibration, harness repair, or replacement of the seat occupancy sensor/mat or related control unit. After repair, the restraint system should be rescanned and the passenger airbag status verified with different seat loads.

communityRecommendations.content: Do not ignore intermittent passenger airbag warnings; owners recommend getting a fault printout while the issue is active because some seat-sensor faults self-clear.
Check for items pressing on or under the passenger seat before service, but if warnings persist, insist on SRS-specific diagnosis rather than a generic code scan.

records.title: HVAC blend door / duo-valve failure (no heat, split-temperature climate)
records.description: W202 climate control has two failure-prone components that produce overlapping symptoms. The blend door actuators (small electric servos behind the dash) develop stripped plastic gears and stop moving the temperature flaps; the duo-valve (monovalve) on the firewall, which gates coolant flow to the heater core, fails open or closed because its internal rubber diaphragm tears. Either fault produces no heat, heat that won't shut off in summer, or — diagnostically classic for the W202 — different temperatures from the driver and passenger vents because the dual-zone system can't equalize. A clogged heater core compounds the problem on neglected cars.
records.solution: Diagnose by listening for the duo-valve solenoids clicking with key on (firewall, driver side). If silent or stuck, replace the duo-valve (~$80-150 part, 30-min DIY job). If the duo-valve cycles but temperature is still wrong, the blend door actuator gears are stripped — actuators are buried in the dash and replacement is labor-intensive (5-8 hours). Flush the heater core with the duo-valve removed to clear sludge before reinstalling. Check the climate control unit (CCU) for cold solder joints if buttons are also unresponsive.
symptoms: No heat in winter (coolant warm but vents blow cold)
Heat won't shut off in summer
Driver and passenger vents blow different temperatures
Climate control unit clicks repeatedly when temperature is changed
Coolant smell or wet passenger floorboard (leaking heater core or duo-valve)
Blower works but airflow direction won't change

records.title: MBUX / Instrument Cluster Black Screen, Rebooting, or No Rear Camera Image
records.description: Owners of the W206 C-Class have reported intermittent or persistent failures of the central MBUX display and digital instrument cluster, including black screens, repeated rebooting, frozen infotainment, and loss of the rear-view camera image. This is well documented through NHTSA complaints and Mercedes service communications tied to software faults and control-unit communication problems on the new electrical architecture. When the display or camera feed drops out, key vehicle information and driver-assistance functions may also be unavailable until the system is restarted or reprogrammed.
records.solution: Diagnosis typically starts with a full vehicle scan for communication faults in the infotainment, camera, and central gateway modules, followed by checking software level and 12V system health. Mercedes repairs commonly involve software updates/reprogramming of MBUX-related control units, replacement of a faulty display/control module if updates do not hold, and verification of camera operation after coding. If symptoms are intermittent, documenting exact conditions and preserving fault logs helps the dealer reproduce the issue.
symptoms: warning messages for inoperative assistance systems
loss of navigation or audio controls

communityRecommendations.content: Before dealer visits, record a video of the screen rebooting or camera failing; intermittent MBUX faults are easier to warranty if the symptom is documented.
Ask the dealer to verify all infotainment and camera control units are on the latest software integration level, not just perform a battery reset.

records.title: Premature Front Brake Squeal, Judder, and Rotor/Pads Replacement
records.description: A recurring owner complaint on the current C-Class is noisy front brakes, vibration under braking, and early rotor/pad replacement despite relatively low mileage. Reports on owner forums and complaint databases describe squeal when cold or at low speed, as well as pulsation or steering-wheel shake from rotor hot spots or uneven pad transfer. The issue appears more common on vehicles used for short trips or with repeated low-speed braking, though some owners report it even with normal driving.
records.solution: Diagnosis should confirm whether the problem is simple pad glazing/noise, rotor thickness variation, or hardware/caliper drag. Repairs range from cleaning and lubricating pad contact points and bedding the brakes properly to replacing front pads and rotors with updated parts if vibration or scoring is present. Wheel torque should be checked after service because uneven torque can worsen brake pulsation.

communityRecommendations.content: Owners commonly recommend a proper brake bedding procedure after pad/rotor replacement to reduce repeat squeal and uneven pad deposits.
If replacing parts out of warranty, ask for coated OE-equivalent rotors and low-dust pads matched to the car's wear sensors.

records.title: 7G-DCT (724.0) Dual-Clutch Transmission Shudder and Mechatronics Failure
records.description: The 7-speed dual-clutch automatic (7G-DCT, transmission code 724.0) fitted to CLA 200/220/250 models develops a noticeable shudder or jolt during low-speed engagement and when shifting from 2nd to 3rd under moderate throttle. Causes include wet multi-plate clutch wear, degraded/contaminated transmission fluid, and failure of the electronic mechatronics (valve body/TCM) unit that controls clutch pressures and gear engagement. Owners also report hard or delayed engagement when coming to a stop and shifting into P/N/R, plus jerky take-off. The DCT is highly sensitive to fluid condition (MB spec 236.21) and outdated control software.
records.solution: Start with a transmission service: full fluid + filter change using MB 236.21 spec oil (recommended every ~60,000 km / 40k miles) and a TCM software update plus clutch adaptation/relearn. Persistent shudder or slipping requires clutch pack replacement; electronic shifting faults and adaptation failures typically require mechatronics (valve body) repair or replacement.
symptoms: Hard or delayed engagement into P/N/R when stopping

records.title: Auxiliary (Backup) Battery Malfunction Warning
records.description: CLA owners frequently see an 'Auxiliary Battery Malfunction' message on the dash. The CLA uses a small secondary 12V battery to support electronics and the start/stop system; it typically degrades after roughly 4-6 years. A weak auxiliary battery, or a charging fault (alternator/voltage regulator, loose connections), triggers the warning and can cause intermittent electrical glitches in the infotainment, lighting and start/stop function, sometimes with a stored 9062 fault.
records.solution: Test and replace the auxiliary battery (a low-cost part located near/behind the engine bay fuse area); clear codes after replacement. If the warning returns, diagnose the charging system — check alternator/voltage regulator output and clean/secure ground and battery connections. Verify the main starter battery health at the same time, as it is the CLA's most common breakdown cause per ADAC data.

records.title: M270/M274 Camshaft Breakage from Defective Weld (Engine Stall) — Safety Recall
records.description: On certain 2015-2016 CLA-Class cars with the 2.0L turbo M270/M274 engine, one or both camshafts were manufactured with a weld outside specification. The defective weld can fail and cause the camshaft to break, damaging the engine, causing sudden loss of power and an engine stall while driving. This is the subject of NHTSA safety recall 15V662 (covering CLA, GLA and SLK). Separately, owners more broadly report camshaft-adjuster rattle/wear on these engines that should not be confused with the recalled welded-camshaft defect.
records.solution: Check the VIN against NHTSA recall 15V662; affected cars receive a free camshaft inspection and replacement at a Mercedes dealer. Any cold-start metallic clatter that persists more than a few seconds or rough running/misfire on an M270/M274 warrants prompt inspection of the camshafts and timing/adjuster components before catastrophic failure.
symptoms: Metallic rattle/clatter from top of engine

records.title: Panoramic Roof Front Panel Detachment — Safety Recall
records.description: On 2014-2020 CLA models the front roof panel located between the windshield and the panoramic sunroof can be improperly bonded, so the adhesive fails and the panel can deteriorate and detach from the vehicle while driving. A detached panel becomes a road hazard for following traffic and increases crash risk. This is covered by two NHTSA recalls (21V197 in 2021 and an expanded 23V854 in 2023).
records.solution: Check the VIN against NHTSA recalls 21V197 and 23V854; affected vehicles receive a free replacement of the front roof panel installed with the correct approved adhesive at a Mercedes dealer. Owners noticing wind noise, lifting, or movement of the front roof trim should have it inspected immediately.

records.title: Premature Rear Brake Wear and Caliper Piston Sticking
records.description: CLA owners report rear brake pads and rotors wearing out before the fronts, with early 'Check Brake Pad Wear' warnings (some as low as ~50k miles) and rear rotor warping/vibration. A commonly cited root cause is the rear caliper piston sticking/dragging — a problem owners and independent mechanics say Mercedes is aware of on CLA and C-Class — which keeps the pad in contact with the rotor, accelerating wear and causing noise. Brake squeal from glazed rotors/worn pads is also common.
records.solution: Replace rear pads and rotors together (new pads on warped/grooved rotors stay noisy), and service or replace any sticking caliper — clean and lubricate slide pins and the piston, or rebuild/replace the caliper if the piston is seized. Apply brake grease to the pad backing/contact points to reduce squeal. Confirm the parking-brake actuator (electric on later cars) is releasing fully.

records.title: Water Leaks into Trunk and Rear Footwell (Vent Flap / Seam Sealing)
records.description: CLA owners report water collecting in the trunk and pooling in the rear footwells, sometimes enough to soak carpets and risk corrosion and electrical faults. A common path is poorly sealing rear pressure-relief vent flaps and water tracking down inside the trunk lid around the tail-light cluster, then into the body. Owners also cite weak factory seam sealer on spot-welded roof/rear upper body panels and door seals that let rainwater seep onto sills.
records.solution: Trace the leak: re-seal or replace the rear vent (pressure-equalization) flaps, reseal the tail-light gaskets and trunk-lid drain/seam areas with appropriate sealant, and inspect/replace door and trunk weatherstrips. Dry out saturated carpet/insulation to prevent mildew and corrosion, and check for related water damage to rear electrical modules.

records.title: 48-Volt Integrated Starter-Generator / DC-DC Converter Failure Causing Warning Messages, Limp Mode, or No Restart
records.description: Owners of six-cylinder CLS 450 models have reported failures in the 48V mild-hybrid system, including the integrated starter-generator, 48V battery support components, or DC-DC converter. Symptoms include 'Stop Vehicle Leave Engine Running,' multiple warning lights, loss of charging support, disabled start/stop, reduced power, and in some cases inability to restart after shutting the car off. This issue is well documented across Mercedes models using the M256/48V architecture and appears in owner complaints and service literature.
records.solution: Perform a full scan of both 12V and 48V systems with Mercedes-capable diagnostics, checking charging voltage, converter operation, and fault memory in the powertrain and energy management modules. Repairs vary by root cause but commonly involve replacing the DC-DC converter, 48V battery, wiring, or the integrated starter-generator assembly, followed by software updates and battery registration/adaptation. Because the system is safety-critical and high-voltage relative to standard 12V systems, diagnosis is best handled by a Mercedes specialist or dealer.
symptoms: stop vehicle leave engine running message

communityRecommendations.content: Do not keep driving on repeated 48V warnings; low converter output can cascade into 12V undervoltage faults and strand the car.
Use a Mercedes-capable scan tool that can read 48V and energy management modules, not just generic OBD-II.

records.title: Front Brake Squeal and Premature Rotor/Pads Wear on AMG-Line and AMG Variants
records.description: Owners of CLS models with larger sport brake packages, especially CLS 450 AMG Line and AMG CLS 53, frequently report persistent front brake squeal, groan at low speeds, and faster-than-expected pad/rotor wear. In many cases the brakes still function normally, but noise and rotor scoring lead to repeated dealer visits. This is a common real-world complaint on Mercedes performance-oriented brake setups using aggressive pad compounds.
records.solution: Inspect pad thickness, rotor runout, rotor surface condition, and caliper slide/piston operation. Mercedes dealers often apply updated pad shims, anti-squeal compound, bedding procedures, or replace pads/rotors if glazing or scoring is present. Using OE-spec friction materials and proper bedding is important; cheap aftermarket pads often worsen noise or dust.

communityRecommendations.content: If the brakes squeal after recent service, ask whether the pads were properly bedded and whether anti-squeal paste/shims were installed.
Owners wanting less dust/noise should stick with reputable OE-equivalent pads rather than the cheapest aftermarket options.

records.title: MBUX / Instrument Cluster Software Freezes, Black Screens, and Backup Camera Malfunctions
records.description: Current-generation CLS models use the widescreen MBUX infotainment and digital cluster system, and owners have reported intermittent screen blackouts, frozen displays, reboot loops, inoperative audio/navigation, and backup camera image failures. Mercedes has issued multiple software updates and service guidance for MBUX-related glitches across this platform. While often software-related, some cases involve display, camera, or control unit replacement when updates do not resolve the issue.
records.solution: Check for stored communication and infotainment faults, verify software level, and apply the latest Mercedes head-unit/instrument cluster updates. If the concern includes a blank reverse camera or persistent black screen, inspect LVDS/video connections, camera module operation, and power/ground integrity before replacing hardware. Battery voltage should also be tested because low system voltage can trigger false MBUX faults.
symptoms: touchpad or steering wheel controls unresponsive

communityRecommendations.content: Ask the dealer to document current software versions before approving expensive hardware replacement; many cases are fixed by programming.
If the backup camera fails intermittently, record a video of the symptom because it often disappears before service appointments.

records.title: Panoramic Sunroof Creaking, Popping, or Binding from Glass/Frame Adjustment and Seal Friction
records.description: A recurring owner complaint on the C257 CLS is noise from the panoramic roof area, especially over driveways, uneven pavement, or in hot/cold weather. The problem is usually not shattered glass but creaking or popping caused by seal friction, roof panel adjustment, or frame movement. Mercedes service departments commonly address it with lubrication, seal treatment, and roof alignment procedures, though some cars need repeat visits.
records.solution: Road-test the vehicle over low-speed body-twist conditions to isolate the roof from interior trim noises. Clean and condition the roof seals, inspect tracks and panel alignment, and perform factory adjustment procedures for the glass and frame if needed. If noise persists, inspect for loose fasteners or worn guide components in the roof cassette.

communityRecommendations.content: Many owners report temporary improvement after cleaning and treating the roof seals with a Mercedes-approved rubber care product.
Reproduce the noise with the shade open and closed to help separate glass/seal noise from headliner trim rattles.

records.title: 48V Integrated Starter-Generator / DC-DC Converter Failure Causing Sudden Power Loss and No-Restart
records.description: Multiple owners of facelift W213 E-Class models with the M256 mild-hybrid system reported sudden warning messages, loss of charging, reduced power, stalling, or a no-start condition traced to the 48V system. Mercedes issued service communications and there are numerous owner complaints describing failure of the integrated starter-generator or associated DC-DC converter/48V battery support hardware. When the 48V system drops offline, the vehicle may illuminate multiple warnings and can become undriveable or fail to restart.
records.solution: Scan the vehicle for 48V powertrain and charging faults, verify 12V and 48V battery state, and inspect freeze-frame data for ISG/DC-DC converter shutdown events. Dealers typically update control-unit software and replace the failed DC-DC converter, integrated starter-generator, or related 48V components as needed. Battery support and proper post-repair coding/adaptation are important to prevent repeat faults.
symptoms: Check engine light or multiple warning lights
Sudden loss of power or limp mode
Engine shuts off at a stop and will not restart

communityRecommendations.content: If buying used, check service history for prior 48V battery, ISG, or DC-DC converter replacement and ask whether the latest powertrain software campaigns were completed.
Owners recommend scanning with a Mercedes-capable tool rather than a generic OBD reader because many 48V faults are stored in submodules not visible to basic scanners.

records.title: Fuel Pump Delivery Module Failure Leading to Extended Crank, Stalling, or No-Start
records.description: A number of late-model E-Class owners reported hard starting, long crank times, hesitation, and occasional stalling traced to low-pressure fuel supply faults, including in-tank fuel pump or delivery module issues. Mercedes service literature for related models and owner reports point to intermittent fuel pressure loss rather than a high-pressure pump problem in some cases. Symptoms can be sporadic at first and become a complete no-start as the pump weakens.
records.solution: Measure low-side fuel pressure during crank and under load, compare commanded versus actual values, and inspect pump current draw and fuel pump control operation. Repair usually involves replacing the in-tank fuel pump/delivery module and sealing ring, then clearing adaptations and verifying pressure stability on a road test. If contaminated fuel is suspected, inspect the tank and filter components as well.
symptoms: Whining noise from fuel tank area

communityRecommendations.content: Owners recommend not ignoring occasional long-crank events; capturing fuel pressure data early can prevent getting stranded later.
Use top-tier fuel and avoid repeatedly running the tank very low, which forum members say may accelerate pump wear from heat.

records.title: MBUX / Instrument Cluster Black Screen, Rebooting, and Rear Camera Inoperative Due to Infotainment Software Faults
records.description: Owners of 2021+ facelift E-Class cars frequently reported MBUX display freezes, black screens, spontaneous reboots, loss of audio/navigation, and backup camera malfunctions. Mercedes has issued software-related service information for MBUX and camera behavior, and NHTSA complaints describe the center display or cluster going dark while driving. In some cases the issue also disables parking aids or leaves the rearview image unavailable when reversing.
records.solution: Confirm software level of the MBUX head unit, instrument cluster, and camera control modules, then perform guided updates and fault tracing. If software does not resolve the issue, dealers may replace the display, head unit, LVDS cable, or camera module depending on stored faults and reproducibility. Low-voltage battery health should also be checked because undervoltage can trigger repeated module resets.
symptoms: No sound from media or phone

communityRecommendations.content: Before replacing hardware, owners recommend checking for pending software updates and documenting the exact conditions when the screen fails so the dealer can reproduce it.
If the issue is intermittent, record a phone video of the black screen or camera failure; forum users say this helps dealers justify module replacement under warranty.

records.title: 12V auxiliary battery malfunction / drain
records.description: EQC owners report recurring 'Auxiliary Battery Malfunction' warnings, sometimes appearing repeatedly (every minute or so), along with dimming lights, intermittent infotainment glitches and occasional no-start. The small 12V auxiliary (AGM) battery that powers electronics weakens or its connections corrode/loosen; because EV electronics constantly draw on it, a marginal 12V battery causes a cascade of warnings. Resting voltage in the ~11.6V range indicates a failing battery.
records.solution: Check and clean/tighten the 12V auxiliary battery terminals first (loose/corroded connectors mimic a dead battery). If resting voltage is low (<12.2V) or faults persist after charging, replace the auxiliary battery with the correct AGM spec, then clear fault codes with a diagnostic tool. Typical replacement is inexpensive.

records.title: Electric drive module coolant leak (motor reducer sealing)
records.description: Due to manufacturing deviations in the electric drive module, the internal cooling circuit can have insufficient sealing, causing coolant to leak — owners likened it to an EV 'oil leak.' If coolant enters the motor it can reduce the high-voltage system's insulation resistance over time; in extreme cases the drive module output power is reduced or the vehicle will not start. This triggered a very large China recall of 10,104 EQCs (later expanded to also cover EQA/EQB) for units built 30 Nov 2018 – 15 Dec 2021.
records.solution: Recall remedy: Mercedes service partners replace the affected electric drivetrain/drive module (a labor-intensive job, quoted up to ~18 hours). Owners outside China with leaks should have the drive unit inspected for coolant seepage under warranty.

records.title: Electric power steering wiring harness water ingress / short circuit
records.description: The wiring harness for the electric power steering (steering control unit) can be damaged during the production process, allowing water/moisture into the harness. This can cause a short circuit and a sudden loss of electric power steering assistance, plus an increased fire risk. Mercedes issued multiple steering-related recall actions for the EQC.
records.solution: Recall remedy: dealer inspects the steering control unit wiring harness and replaces it if damaged, at no cost. Drivers get a red instrument-cluster warning before failure in many cases; the vehicle should be taken in immediately if shown.

records.title: Heavy cold-weather range loss and inefficient heat pump
records.description: EQC owners report large winter range drops — commonly 25-30%+ at around -10C, with real-world examples falling from ~230-239 miles to ~180-190 miles. While some cold-weather loss is normal for any EV, owners and reviewers single out the EQC's heat-pump/PTC heater strategy as relatively inefficient (the car leans on the energy-hungry PTC heaters rather than the heat pump), and the EQC lacks the flexible departure preconditioning of some rivals, making winter range management hands-on. Independent Norwegian cold testing measured ~25% loss.
records.solution: Not a defect with a single fix — mitigate by preculating/preconditioning the cabin and battery while plugged in, using seat/steering-wheel heating instead of cabin heat, and selecting eco/range modes. records.title: High-voltage battery housing corrosion from inadequate sealing
records.description: On early 2019-built EQC 400 4Matic vehicles, the high-voltage traction battery housing was not adequately corrosion-protected/sealed at the factory. Moisture can penetrate the housing and corrode internal components and electrical connections. In the worst case the vehicle cannot be restarted, and there is an elevated fire risk. records.solution: Mercedes recall remedy: dealer inspects the high-voltage battery housing and, where required, replaces the battery or applies corrosion-protection/sealing measures at no cost. Owners should run a VIN recall check before buying a used 2019 EQC and confirm the fix was performed.

records.title: Inconsistent brake-by-wire pedal feel (regen/friction blending)
records.description: Owners widely report a non-linear, inconsistent brake pedal: 'spongy' or 'mushy' at the top of travel then suddenly 'grabby' lower down, making smooth stops hard. This is a recognized trait across Mercedes EQ models, not a one-off defect.

Software updates have been applied to improve blending; persistent judder/noise should be diagnosed at a dealer (brake control unit / actuator checks). Owners can also adjust regen via the steering-wheel paddles to suit their driving.

records.title: Side-impact crash sensor connector not latched (airbag/safety system fault)

records.solution: Recall remedy: dealer inspects and correctly latches/secures the side crash sensor connectors (and replaces if needed) at no cost. An airbag/restraint warning lamp may illuminate if the connection has dropped.

records.title: AIRMATIC Air Suspension Clunks and Premature Rear Shock/Damper Wear
records.description: EQS owners report low-speed clunking over bumps, uneven ride height, and a ride quality that drifts from floaty to harsh as mileage builds, traced to the AIRMATIC air-suspension system (worn sway-bar links, bushings, air struts, or compressor/valve-block degradation). On EQS SUVs in particular, premature rear shock-absorber/damper replacement has been documented, often within the first one to two years, accompanied by noise and degraded comfort. The very heavy curb weight combined with rear-axle steering also accelerates inside-edge tire wear when alignment drifts. These are wear/durability concerns rather than safety recalls but can be expensive once out of warranty.
records.solution: Have the suspension inspected for a leaking air strut, failing compressor/valve block, or worn sway-bar links/bushings when clunks or ride-height faults appear; address AIRMATIC malfunction messages promptly before a leak burns out the compressor. Replace failed rear shocks/dampers (often under warranty or service bulletin early on). Keep the car on an annual alignment to limit inside-edge tire wear from the heavy weight and rear-axle steering.

records.title: Battery Management System Software Overload Triggers High-Voltage Shutdown (NHTSA 24V372000)
records.description: On a large population of EQ vehicles, continuous diagnostic requests from other onboard control units can overload the battery management system's (BMS) memory capacity. This causes the BMS to open the high-voltage contactors, disconnecting the battery pack from the powertrain and producing a sudden loss of drive power. Mercedes-Benz USA recalled 14,912 EQE/EQS/EQE SUV/EQS SUV vehicles in June 2024 (NHTSA campaign 24V372000). Unlike many EQ software fixes, this remedy could not be delivered over the air and required a dealer visit, making it a recurring frustration for owners. The same BMS software is used on EU-spec cars.
records.solution: An authorized Mercedes-Benz dealer must reprogram the battery management system software; this cannot be done via OTA update. Owners should verify VIN against recall 24V372000 and schedule the dealer reflash. Until corrected, a high-voltage shutdown can occur with little warning, so prompt completion is advised.
symptoms: Vehicle shuts down / will not move

records.title: Electric Drivetrain Software Fault Causing Sudden Loss of Propulsion (NHTSA 23V405000)
records.description: A software error in the electric drivetrain's fault-management logic can deactivate the electric drive unit while driving, causing a sudden loss of drive power. Mercedes-Benz discovered the issue in October 2022 after a field report of an electrical drivetrain malfunction, and issued a U.S. recall (NHTSA campaign 23V405000) in July 2023 covering 8,281 vehicles. The fault-management software reacts incorrectly to drive-unit connector contact issues and shuts down propulsion as a precaution. This is a meaningful safety concern because power can be lost in traffic. EU-spec EQS vehicles run the same drivetrain software and were addressed in parallel manufacturer software recalls.
records.solution: Mercedes dealers reflash the electric drivetrain control software free of charge under the recall; no hardware replacement is typically required. Owners can check VIN against the recall at the NHTSA or Mercedes-Benz recall portals and have the update applied. If a loss-of-power event occurs, the vehicle should be brought in promptly for diagnosis and the latest drivetrain software.
symptoms: Sudden loss of drive power while driving

records.title: Flush/Retractable Door Handles Fail to Present, Locking Owners Out
records.description: The EQS uses electrically presenting flush door handles that pop out as the driver approaches. Owners widely report handles that fail to extend, require multiple pulls, or do not present at all, occasionally locking the owner out of the car. The handles are not heated and can freeze solid in winter, and forcing a frozen handle can damage the presentation motor. Some failures are software glitches (handle won't present on touch but works with the key fob), while others are mechanical/motor failures, with several owners reporting repeat handle replacements within months. This is a known issue across the keyless-go Mercedes range and is highly relevant in cold EU climates.
records.solution: If a handle won't present but the key fob still operates the door, the cause is usually software; a 12V battery disconnect/reset for ~15 minutes often restores function, and a dealer software update may be needed. For frozen handles, carefully de-ice rather than forcing them, and use the owner's-manual emergency unlock (mechanical key in the door) to avoid lockout. Mechanically failed handles or presentation motors are replaced individually; budget several hundred dollars per handle out of warranty.
symptoms: Requires multiple pulls to open door
Handle works with key fob but not on approach

records.title: MBUX Hyperscreen Freezing, Blackouts and Random Reboots
records.description: The 56-inch MBUX Hyperscreen and central display are a frequent complaint among EQS owners, who report lag, frozen screens, full blackouts and random reboots, especially on early 2022-2023 cars. A frozen Hyperscreen temporarily disables navigation, charge planning, climate control and the reversing/360 camera view, which is a real usability and safety annoyance. German owners on motor-talk.de have documented total MBUX failures mid-trip (e.g. a complete blackout during a Switzerland-Poland drive). Over-the-air updates frequently stall partway and sometimes require the car to sit at a dealer for a manual flash. Most cases are software rather than a hardware defect, though heat exposure and rare failing display hardware are also cited.
records.solution: Try a soft reset by holding the central display power/volume control, or perform a 12V battery disconnect for ~15 minutes to force a system restart. Keep MBUX software current; if an OTA update hangs, the dealer can cancel and re-push or manually flash the unit. Persistent blackouts that survive a reset warrant a dealer diagnosis for a possible display/head-unit hardware replacement (a four-figure part out of warranty).
symptoms: Loss of navigation and climate controls

records.title: Recurring 'Battery Malfunction / Do Not Tow' Warning and Front Motor Interlock Faults
records.description: Many EQS and EQS SUV owners report frequent 'Battery Malfunction' and 'Malfunction - Towing is not permitted' (Do Not Tow) dashboard messages, in some cases once or twice a month during the first 20,000 miles. The message appears to be a catch-all for several underlying conditions. In milder cases the car still drives and the warning self-clears or resolves with an ignition/12V reset; in severe cases the car refuses to shift into Drive, Neutral or Reverse and is immobilized. A subset of these events trace to a front electric motor 'interlock' fault that prevented the car from being put in Park and required Mercedes to replace the front electric drive motor under warranty. Owners frequently note multiple dealer visits and long parts waits before resolution.
records.solution: For a transient warning, switch the car off, wait ~5 minutes, then restart; if that fails, a 12V battery disconnect/reset often clears it. Persistent or shift-inhibiting faults require dealer diagnosis: many are resolved with battery/drivetrain software updates (often bundled with the BMS and drivetrain recalls), while a confirmed front-motor interlock fault requires replacement of the front electric drive unit under the EV powertrain warranty.
symptoms: 'Do Not Tow' / 'Towing is not permitted' message
Vehicle will not go into Park

records.title: 9G-Tronic / AMG Speedshift Harsh or Jerky Shifting Requiring Adaptation
records.description: W463A G-Class models (G 550 with 9G-Tronic 725.0, AMG G 63 with AMG Speedshift TCT 9G) are reported for harsh, jerky, or hesitant gear changes - notably a sudden jolt on certain up/downshifts and shudder at low speeds in stop-and-go traffic. The wet-clutch take-up element and learned clutch-fill adaptations can drift out of spec, and degraded/low ATF or post-repair software mismatches aggravate the symptom. Often improvable without hardware replacement.
records.solution: First verify ATF level, condition and correct specification; service fluid and filter (a practical interval is roughly every 40,000-50,000 miles, sooner with heavy/off-road or towing use). Perform the factory standstill/clutch adaptation reset with a compatible scan tool and apply any TCU software updates. Persistent harshness after adaptation may indicate valve body / conductor-plate or clutch-pack wear.

records.title: Body, Tailgate and Underbody Frame Corrosion
records.description: The hand-built W463 body (Magna Steyr, Graz) is widely documented for rust because the panel metallurgy and rust-proofing are little changed from the late-1970s design. Common corrosion sites are the rear tailgate (especially the lower section around the spare-tire mount), door bottoms, sills/rocker areas, window/windscreen weatherstrip channels that trap water, and the rear frame tubes and rear strut/shock mounts on the ladder chassis. Frame-tube and strut-mount corrosion is a structural safety concern on older/salt-belt examples, distinct from the cosmetic body rust.
records.solution: Inspect the tailgate lower edge, door bottoms, sills, and especially the rear frame tubes and strut mounts; sandblast and treat or weld in repair panels before rust spreads. Preventatively apply cavity wax (Waxoyl) inside doors and underbody, wash off road salt after winter, and keep trim-clip and weatherstrip drainage clear. Severe frame corrosion may require frame section repair rather than full-frame replacement.
symptoms: Visible rust on sills and door bottoms

records.title: Front Axle Wiring Harness Chafe Against Oil Cooler Causing ABS/ESC Loss (Recall 23V097000)
records.description: NHTSA recall 23V097000 covers 2019-2021 G 550 and AMG G 63 vehicles in which the front axle wiring harness can chafe against an oil cooler and become damaged. The resulting damage can cause loss of anti-lock braking (ABS) and electronic stability control (ESC), increasing crash risk. 26,116 units were affected; owner notification letters were mailed April 10, 2023.
records.solution: Have the recall remedy performed at a Mercedes-Benz dealer free of charge: the harness is inspected and either a protective sleeve is installed or the front axle wiring harness is replaced as necessary. Verify completion via NHTSA VIN lookup, especially on used purchases.

records.title: Fuel Pump Impeller Deformation Causing Loss of Drive Power (Recall 23V445000)

records.title: M157 5.5L Biturbo V8 Cylinder Scoring and Camshaft Adjuster Wear (Pre-Facelift G 63)
records.description: The 5.5L M157 biturbo V8 used in the W463 AMG G 63 before the 2019 redesign is documented for cylinder wall scoring/scuffing at higher mileage plus weaknesses in timing-chain components and camshaft (VVT) adjusters. The camshaft adjuster magnets/solenoids meter oil to the VVT and chain; restricted flow accelerates chain and gear wear. Oil intrusion into the camshaft position sensor wiring can also mimic internal engine faults. Symptoms range from multi-cylinder misfires to rattle and, in worst cases, metal in the oil from bore scoring.
records.solution: Use only the correct AMG-spec synthetic oil and shorter change intervals. Diagnose misfires by checking camshaft adjusters/solenoids and cleaning oil-contaminated sensor connectors before assuming internal failure. Inspect timing chain, tensioner and sprockets; replace worn camshaft adjusters. Confirmed cylinder scoring requires major engine work or replacement.

records.title: M177 4.0L Twin-Turbo V8 Excessive Oil Consumption and Cylinder Scoring
records.description: The 4.0L biturbo M177 V8 in the W463A G 550 and AMG G 63 is documented for above-normal engine oil consumption (often 1 quart per ~1,000-2,000 miles in worse cases), with the most severe outcome being cylinder bore/liner scoring and piston ring wear at higher mileage. The high-output, hot-running twin-turbo design stresses piston rings and the iron-coated aluminum bores; carbon buildup and ring coking aggravate consumption. If left unaddressed, low oil level can lead to bearing/piston damage. Owners report repeated low-oil warnings between services and, in advanced cases, misfires and blue exhaust smoke.
records.solution: Check oil level frequently and top up with the correct MB 229.5/AMG-spec full-synthetic oil; do not rely solely on service intervals. Diagnose with an oil-consumption test and leak-down/compression test; rule out the common contributors first (PCV/oil separator diaphragm, valve seals, turbo seals). Walnut-blast intake valves if carbon-fouled. Confirmed cylinder scoring requires a short block or engine replacement, ideally under powertrain warranty.

records.title: OM642 3.0L V6 Diesel Oil Cooler Seal Leak (G 350 CDI / G 350 d)
records.description: European-market diesel G-Class models with the OM642 3.0L V6 (G 320 CDI / G 350 CDI / G 350 d) commonly develop oil leaks from the engine oil cooler seals seated in the valley of the engine block. The original orange seals harden from heat and shrink, allowing oil to weep down the back of the block. Mercedes upgraded to purple Viton seals (~2010+), which reduced but did not eliminate the problem. Because the cooler sits under the intake, the leak is often misdiagnosed and the repair is labor-intensive.
records.solution: Replace the oil cooler O-ring/gasket seals (use the updated Viton seals) and inspect the cooler itself for damage. While the intake is removed, it is cost-effective to also service the swirl-flap linkage and clean the EGR. Confirm the leak source versus turbo pedestal and valve cover gaskets, which can leak simultaneously.
symptoms: Oil staining at rear of engine block

records.title: OM642 Diesel Intake Manifold Swirl Flap (Runner) Failure
records.description: On diesel G-Class models with the OM642 V6, the plastic intake-manifold swirl flap linkage becomes brittle and snaps, and the swirl-flap actuator motor can fail (often after being contaminated by oil weeping from the turbo inlet seal). The broken plastic rods can also be drawn into the engine in worst cases. This is a well-known weak point that triggers intake-runner control faults, limp mode, and emissions test failures. Particularly relevant to higher-mileage EU diesel examples.
records.solution: Replace the swirl-flap actuator and fit a metal/upgraded swirl-flap repair kit (e.g. updated connecting rod kit) to replace the brittle plastic linkage. Address any upstream turbo oil leak contaminating the motor. A resistor bypass only clears the code and is not a proper repair if the linkage is broken.

records.title: 12V Battery Parasitic Drain / No-Start After Sitting
records.description: GLA owners frequently report a dead 12V battery and no-start after the car sits, caused by parasitic drain. Documented contributors include a control module (e.g., signal acquisition module) failing to enter sleep mode, a relay rapidly cycling when the car is off, and 'intelligent' alternator charging strategies that under-charge a battery on short trips. On the GLA 250e/48V-equipped cars, auxiliary/12V supply faults can also cause complete power loss. The drain leaves owners stranded and can trigger cascading electrical warnings.
records.solution: Perform a parasitic draw test (current with vehicle asleep), isolate the offending circuit/module by pulling fuses, and replace the faulty relay or module that won't sleep. Verify charging-system health and replace a worn 12V battery (and the auxiliary battery where fitted), then re-register the battery via diagnostics. Latest module/software updates address some sleep-mode faults.
symptoms: Dead battery / no crank after sitting

records.title: 7G-DCT (724.0) Dual-Clutch Transmission Shudder & Mechatronics Failure
records.description: The X156 GLA's 7G-DCT 7-speed wet dual-clutch transmission (type 724.0) is prone to low-speed shudder/judder, jerky or delayed engagement, and clutch slip, typically emerging from ~40,000-75,000 mi (60,000-120,000 km). Root causes are wet multi-plate clutch wear, degraded/contaminated DCT fluid, and failure of the mechatronics control unit that manages clutch pressures. Stop-go urban driving and skipped fluid services accelerate it. Once shuddering begins, worn clutch packs can progress to a no-drive condition within a few thousand km.
records.solution: First step is a DCT fluid (DCTF) and filter change with a STAR/XENTRY clutch adaptation reset; this often clears early shudder. Persistent slip/jerk requires clutch pack replacement, and an internal-failure mechatronics unit must be replaced and re-coded. Mercedes addressed some early cars via TCU software updates. Use only the specified DCTF and adhere to the ~40k mi adaptation/60k km fluid intervals.
symptoms: Low-speed shudder or vibration when pulling away

records.title: Diesel EGR/DPF Clogging & AdBlue (SCR) System Faults (OM651/OM654)
records.description: GLA diesels (GLA 200d/220d), popular in Germany and the EU, develop clogged EGR valves and diesel particulate filters from soot buildup, plus AdBlue/SCR (NOx reduction) faults. EGR carbon fouling causes rough idle, reduced power and emissions faults; DPF blockage triggers limp mode if regeneration can't complete (common with short urban trips). AdBlue/SCR issues include crystallization from irregular use, sensor/NOx-sensor faults, level/quality warnings and countdown-to-no-start messages. The OM651 also shares timing-chain-stretch tendencies.
records.solution: Carry out periodic motorway runs to allow active DPF regeneration; clean or replace a clogged EGR valve and clear/replace a blocked DPF. SCR faults require diagnosing and replacing NOx sensors, the SCR/AdBlue metering/dosing unit, or clearing crystallization, then resetting the no-start countdown via XENTRY. Use only fresh, correct-spec AdBlue and keep the tank topped.
symptoms: Check engine and DPF warning lights

records.title: M270/M274 Timing Chain Stretch & Tensioner Wear (Cold-Start Rattle)
records.description: The GLA's M270/M274 turbo four-cylinder petrol engines are widely documented to suffer timing chain elongation and tensioner/guide wear, usually presenting between roughly 40,000-80,000 mi. A loose chain produces a distinctive rattle for the first few seconds after a cold start until oil pressure loads the tensioner. A related defect is the camshaft tone/reluctor ring slipping, throwing timing-correlation faults. Left unaddressed, a stretched chain can jump time and cause valve-to-piston contact and major engine damage.
records.solution: Confirm with live cam/crank correlation data; replace the timing chain, tensioner, and guides as a set (and the camshaft sprockets/tone ring if the ring has slipped). Strict adherence to short oil-change intervals with correct-spec oil slows wear. German specialists recommend chain inspection/replacement around 100,000-150,000 km on these engines.

records.title: MBUX/COMAND Infotainment Black Screen & Reboot (NHTSA Recall 21V354)
records.description: GLA infotainment units suffer black/frozen screens and spontaneous reboots. On H247 cars this is the NVIDIA-Tegra-based MBUX head unit, which can fail to boot or reboot ~50 seconds after startup, disabling the rearview camera image (the basis of NHTSA recall 21V354 covering 2019-2021 MB models including the GLA). Weak 12V battery voltage dips and heat aggravate it.
